input.quote: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions.
input.rationale: § 14.3 selects the substantive laws of the State of New York, which is the playbook's preferred governing law. There is no arbitration clause anywhere in the document (search for "arbitration" returns nothing), and no foreign venue or vendor-home-jurisdiction forum is imposed, so the walk-away scenario is absent. The related dispute mechanics (§ 14.4 mutual jury-trial waiver and § 14.14 two-year actions period) are mutual and do not affect the governing-law analysis. The only point short of the preferred wording is that the clause is silent on venue — it does not expressly confer exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County. That is a missing sub-mechanic rather than a material failure (disputes would still be litigated in courts, not foreign arbitration), so we note it rather than redline; if the clause is reopened for other reasons we would add exclusive New York County venue.
